Answers.content: The time interval used in this rate of change calculation is between the years 2018 and 2019. Yes, it should be explicitly defined as 1 year for clarity and consistency in calculations.

The unit of time for the rate of change calculation should be explicitly defined as 1 year. This ensures clarity and accuracy in interpreting the rate of change between any two consecutive years in the given data.

The definition of "rate of change" used in this calculation refers to the average rate of change over the given time interval. Specifically, it measures how much the number of students receiving scholarships changed per year between 2018 and 2019.

To calculate the average rate of change, you would use the formula:

\[
\text{Average Rate of Change} = \frac{\Delta y}{\Delta t} = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{t_2 - t_1}
\]

where \( y_1 \) and \( y_2 \) are the values of students receiving scholarships in 2018 and 2019, respectively, and \( t_1 \) and \( t_2 \) are the corresponding years.

In this case:

- \( y_1 = 36 \) (students in 2018)
- \( y_2 = 22 \) (students in 2019)
- \( t_1 = 2018 \)
- \( t_2 = 2019 \)

The time interval between 2018 and 2019 is 1 year. Therefore, the rate of change should indeed be explicitly defined as the average rate of change over this one-year interval to ensure clarity in the calculation.
